classes.name: Levothyroxine (T4)
classes.description: Levothyroxine sodium: generic tablets and the brands Synthroid, Levoxyl, Unithroid, Euthyrox; Tirosint capsules; oral solutions Tirosint-SOL, Thyquidity, Ermeza. Generic tablets are AB-rated to specific reference brands, so a brand-only rule matters. Not liothyronine or desiccated thyroid.
classes.plainDescription: The standard daily pill that replaces thyroid hormone when your thyroid is underactive.

classes.name: Liothyronine (T3) and desiccated thyroid
classes.description: Liothyronine (Cytomel, generic tablets) and desiccated thyroid (Armour Thyroid, NP Thyroid; unapproved drugs under FDA enforcement action, often non-formulary; Adthyza reportedly discontinued). Levothyroxine is never this class's pick.
classes.plainDescription: Other thyroid pills, used alongside or instead of levothyroxine in some patients.

preferredAgent.sig: Healthy adults: full replacement about 1.6 mcg/kg once daily. Older adults or heart disease: start 12.5 to 25 mcg daily and raise by 12.5 to 25 mcg every 6 to 8 weeks. Adjust to TSH. Take on an empty stomach 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast (label).
preferredAgent.sigShort: Start per weight/age, titrate to TSH
preferredAgent.plainSig: One pill every morning on an empty stomach, 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast. Your dose is adjusted by blood tests.
